cards.text: This passage is six verses, friend. I've had batches in the oven longer than that, and it still hits HARD. A man with leprosy comes to Jesus, drops to his knees and starts begging.

cards.question: The leper on his knees begs Jesus to make him ___.

cards.text: Now listen to HOW he asks. He's already sure Jesus CAN do it. His 'if' is about something else.

cards.question: The leper is sure Jesus can make him clean. What is his 'if' about?

cards.text: Jesus looks at this man down on his knees, and He is moved with compassion.

cards.question: Moved with compassion, Jesus heals the leper from a distance, without touching him.

cards.text: Jesus reaches out His hand and touches the man. “I am willing,” He says. “Be clean!”

cards.question: When Jesus tells the leper “Be clean!” the leprosy leaves him right away.

cards.text: Leprosy GONE. Immediately. Friend, I can't get dough to rise that fast. Then Jesus promptly sends the man away, with a stern warning on his way out.

cards.question: Jesus sends the healed man away with a stern warning. What is the warning?
Jesus tells the healed man to go show himself to the ___ and present the offering ___ prescribed for his cleansing.
Why does Jesus send the healed man to the priest with that offering?

answers.text: To ask for the priest's blessing
To pay the priest for the healing

cards.text: Then the healed man heads out, clean, with a priest to go see. Me? My first day out of that junk drawer, I just stood on my gold base blinking at the light.

cards.question: The healed man keeps the news to himself, just like Jesus told him.

cards.text: Nope. He goes out and openly proclaims it and spreads the news. Honestly, if somebody pulled ME out of that junk drawer, I'd have told the DUST.

cards.question: Now that the healed man is spreading the news, what changes for Jesus?

answers.text: He can't enter a town in plain view
He has to send the crowds away
He has to cross the sea by boat

cards.question: So Jesus stays out in solitary places. What happens out there?

answers.text: People come to Him from every quarter
He finally gets some time alone
The priests come out to question Him

findings.problem: Non-opening story cards 3, 7, 9 and 15 contain three, three, four and three sentences respectively, counting the quoted sentences on card 7. Each exceeds the two-sentence maximum.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The distractor “Whether God will allow it” is too close to “Whether Jesus is willing.” Both can be understood as uncertainty about divine consent, so a baker could reasonably defend the distractor as correct.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on luck rather than the earlier cards: how Jesus heals (6), the immediate timing (8), the warning's content (10), the priest and Moses details (11), the offering's purpose (12), and whether the man obeys (14) are not inferable from their setups. Six of the ten choice cards are discovery questions, so most choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Neither blank can be reasoned out from the earlier cards, which have not introduced the priest, Moses or the cleansing instructions. The blanks ask for wording and details the baker has not seen rather than meaning supported by the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
